The color of a common crow is black.

To enhance the artistic concept of this interactive gallery, we can deepen the multi-sensory immersion by aligning the olfactory, auditory, and tactile elements with specific historical art movements. For the Renaissance room, the scented mist could evoke aged parchment and beeswax, paired with the warm, resonant tones of a lute or harpsichord, while the textured rugs mimic the heavy velvet drapes of the era. In the Impressionist wing, the air might carry the fresh scent of rain on wet cobblestones and blooming lilacs, accompanied by the light, flowing melodies of Debussy, with soft, woven silk curtains inviting a gentle touch. Finally, the Modernist section could utilize crisp, metallic scents like ozone or ink, set against minimalist electronic or avant-garde classical compositions, with rough-hewn wool rugs that ground the visitor in the stark reality of the present moment. This cohesive approach ensures that every sense contributes to a unified narrative, transforming passive viewing into an embodied experience.
